implementation: ACPIPLAT owns exact MADT UID/APIC mapping and bounded CST/CSD/LPI parsing. All-CPU CST parity, duplicate CPU objects, package/resource encoding and unsupported coordination/context are checked before copying an immutable declaration.

A present LPI has independent source/count/index/minimum/wake-latency/context fields; no inherited CST type/method/hint/coordination/power. The source tag distinguishes CST entry-plus-exit latency from LPI worst-case wake latency; both use microseconds. Present malformed CSD/LPI requirements also block otherwise eligible peers while dependency scope is unknown. Unrelated Notify81 is ignored; related CPU/container notification withdraws the old catalogue.

CPUPOWER owns initial bounded idle intent (100us declared entry/exit cap, target4 times declared latency). It is independent of PowerService frequency profiles, adds no worker/idle callback and writes no enabling MSR.

Kernel local admission requires native Intel/family6, actual MONITOR and CPUID5 extensions/masked interrupt break/substate, ARAT, invariant TSC, protected actual MONITOR_FSM read, actual WB monitor page and armed continuing local LAPIC timer with remaining budget.

One permanent isolated WB page per CPU; actual PTE/PAT/effective-MTRR confirmation uses a nonblocking page-table try-guard. No allocation/remapping, AML/module callback or Runtime owner spans MWAIT. A final monitored check repeats due-absolute/Ready/epoch/lifecycle/timer admission.

Descriptor/policy withdrawal closes admission, stores the monitored word and sends the existing wake IPI, retaining exact active exits before teardown. After MWAIT the active pin is released and STI/NOP/CLI delivers the pending wake IRQ before timer leave/rearm. HLT fallback remains functional.

Independent fixed Descriptor96/Policy32/Info192 and optional DriverCpuPowerApi184/R4DEV29-656 tails preserve all prior records/slots. SYSINFO CPUIDLE reads passive source-specific declarations and software counts; unavailable fields are explicit. Cached local eligibility is no current hardware residency claim.
